summary.text: Mike Kennedy is the Republican incumbent seeking re-election in Utah's newly drawn 4th District after representing the old 3rd District since January 2025. A family physician and attorney who served in both chambers of the Utah Legislature, he sits on the Natural Resources, Transportation and Infrastructure, and Science, Space, and Technology committees. His House website says he is focused on fiscal responsibility, border security and pushing back against federal overreach.

paragraphs.text: Kennedy was born in Lansing, Michigan, and his House website says he was raised by a single mother alongside six siblings and held his first job at age 12.
He served a two-year mission for The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints and then earned a bachelor's degree from Brigham Young University.

He received an M.D. from Michigan State University in 1998 and became a family physician, and later earned a J.D. from Brigham Young University's J. Reuben Clark Law School in 2007, a degree his House website says he pursued to better advocate for his patients.
His career experience includes work as a family doctor, attorney and small business owner.
Kennedy was elected to the Utah House of Representatives, District 27, and served from 2013 to 2019, keeping his family medicine practice while in office.
In 2018 he sought the Republican nomination for U.S. Senate and lost the June 26 primary to Mitt Romney, 71.3% to 28.7%.

He returned to the legislature as a member of the Utah State Senate from 2021 to 2025, representing District 14 and then District 21, and chaired the Senate Health and Human Services Committee from 2021 to 2024.
In 2024 Kennedy won the June 25 Republican primary for Utah's 3rd District with 38.8% in a five-candidate field, then won the general election with 66.4%, and he was sworn in in January 2025.

In the 119th Congress (2025-2026) he serves on the Committee on Natural Resources, where he is vice chair of the Federal Lands subcommittee and also sits on the Indian and Insular Affairs subcommittee, as well as on the Committee on Transportation and Infrastructure and the Committee on Science, Space, and Technology.
His House website says he has been married to his wife, Katrina, for 35 years and that they have raised eight children and have 12 grandchildren.
